knowledge:
- key_parameters: method="exhaustive" for up to 4 signaling genes, "greedy" for 5 or more ;; global=logical, if FALSE detailed results are plotted for specific double knock-out pairs ;; ind=index of the specific double knock-out pair to plot when global is FALSE
- alternatives: nem package=classic Nested Effects Models, preferred when there are no double knockouts ;; B-NEM package=general Boolean network inference from combinatorial perturbations, preferred for general Boolean networks but slower than epiNEM ;; ARACNE or PC algorithm=faster network inference methods but cannot derive logical gates in the network structure
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing knock-out screen data containing both single and double perturbations (e.g., binary differential expression matrices) to infer epistatic relationships (logical gates) and downstream effect reporter attachments.
- pitfalls: Exhaustive search is computationally expensive and only feasible for up to 4 signaling genes; greedy search must be used for 5 or more. Input data must be binary (0/1), typically derived by thresholding differential expression p-values and fold changes.

workflows.name: small_gene_set_inference
workflows.intent: Infer the epistatic network structure and logical gates for a small set of signaling genes.
input: binary_effects_matrix.csv (binary matrix with effect reporters as rows and single/double perturbations as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare binary effect matrix ;; 2. Run epiNEM network inference ;; 3. Plot the inferred network structure
workflows.code:
data <- matrix(sample(c(0,1), 100*4, replace = TRUE), 100, 4)
colnames(data) <- c("A", "A.B", "B", "C")
rownames(data) <- paste("E", 1:100, sep = "_")
print(head(data))
res <- epiNEM(data, method = "exhaustive")
plot(res)

workflows.name: systematic_modulator_screening
workflows.intent: Perform a systematic analysis to identify and rank the most likely modulators for signaling gene pairs across a larger perturbation screen.
input: large_binary_effects_matrix.csv (binary matrix with effect reporters as rows and multiple single/double perturbations as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare binary effect matrix ;; 2. Run epiScreen to identify modulators ;; 3. Plot global distribution of inferred logics ;; 4. Plot detailed ranked modulators for specific pairs ;; 5. Visualize perfect binary effects matrix for each logic
workflows.code:
data <- matrix(sample(c(0,1), 100*9, replace = TRUE), 100, 9)
colnames(data) <- c("A.B", "A.C", "B.C", "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "G")
rownames(data) <- paste("E", 1:100, sep = "_")
res <- epiScreen(data)
plot(res)
plot(res, global = FALSE, ind = 1)
epiAnno()
